title: Artifact URIs that make the server connect to a named host must pass the trusted-host policy
answers: tracking server connects to arbitrary host through artifact_location (SSRF)
why does mlflow server reject an ftp, sftp, hdfs or http artifact location
model version source on another host is refused with 400
body:
Symptom: a client creating an experiment, workspace or model version with an ftp/sftp/hdfs/viewfs/http(s)/mlflow-artifacts/r2/b2/abfss location makes the tracking server open connections to that host when it later reads or uploads artifacts.
Root cause: mlflow/store/artifact/artifact_repository_registry.py:ArtifactRepositoryRegistry.get_artifact_repository dereferenced stored URIs with no destination check, and the handlers in mlflow/server/handlers.py built repositories from stored locations directly.
Fix pattern: Pass every submitted or stored host-addressed URI through mlflow/store/artifact/host_policy.py:rejected_host_addressed_scheme. Acceptance uses handlers.py:_validate_artifact_uri_scheme (field-specific 400); fetch uses handlers.py:_get_artifact_repository_for_uri. Do not call get_artifact_repository on stored locations without one of these.
Constraints: Trusted targets are the hosts of ARTIFACT_ROOT and ARTIFACTS_DESTINATION only, or a scheme listed in MLFLOW_ALLOWED_HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES. Ports are normalized to the scheme default before comparison, a portless hdfs URI matches only a portless root (fail closed), and an authority with a backslash or whitespace is never trusted. The registry check runs only when is_tracking_server_process() is true; client processes are unaffected. Proxied http roots under --serve-artifacts never reach the handler guard. A scheme that connects to the URI host must be added to HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES.
Applies: Server-side artifact URI acceptance and repository construction; not client-side logging.
applies: Server-process artifact URI acceptance and repository construction in mlflow/server and mlflow/store/artifact; client code paths are not covered.

Allow specifying trusted external hosts for experiment and model artifact storage
New workspace rejects custom remote artifact storage schemes with a server error
search: Server-side artifact URIs specifying remote hosts must be validated against a trusted-host policy via mlflow/store/artifact/host_policy.py:rejected_host_addressed_scheme. Handlers use _validate_artifact_uri_scheme to return 400 on invalid submissions and _get_artifact_repository_for_uri on fetch, forbidding direct calls to ArtifactRepositoryRegistry.get_artifact_repository on stored locations. Trusted hosts are limited to ARTIFACT_ROOT, ARTIFACTS_DESTINATION, or schemes configured in MLFLOW_ALLOWED_HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES, rejecting authorities containing backslashes or whitespace. Enforcement applies only in tracking server processes (is_tracking_server_process() is true) during URI acceptance and repository construction, not client logging or proxied --serve-artifacts roots.
